name: Duolingo
tagline: The most downloaded education app uses behavioral science to make language learning addictive — but the Hook Model starts breaking after Day 14.
key_insight: Duolingo is a masterclass in habit formation mechanics but struggles with the transition from extrinsic hooks to intrinsic motivation. The streak counter keeps users opening the app, but 'opening the app' ≠ 'learning a language.' Products that confuse engagement metrics with outcome metrics eventually face this tension.
top_technique: Streak Mechanics as Loss Aversion Engine
top_evidence: Streak-based users have 2.3x higher DAU/MAU (Duolingo 2024 shareholder letter). Variable ratio reinforcement via leaderboard + XP creates slot-machine engagement patterns.

techniques.title: Streak Mechanics as Loss Aversion Engine
techniques.description: Duolingo's streak counter exploits Kahneman & Tversky's finding that losses feel ~2x heavier than gains. A 30-day streak creates massive psychological cost to breaking it — users don't practice to learn, they practice to avoid loss. The Streak Freeze power-up monetizes this anxiety directly.
techniques.evidence: Duolingo's 2024 shareholder letter: streak-based users have 2.3x higher DAU/MAU ratio. Streak Freeze is the #2 monetized feature after Super Duolingo.

techniques.title: Variable Ratio Reinforcement Schedule
techniques.description: XP rewards, league positions, and achievement unlocks follow variable ratio schedules — the same pattern that makes slot machines engaging. Users never know exactly when the next 'celebration' will trigger, creating persistent checking behavior.
techniques.evidence: B.F. Skinner's research shows variable ratio schedules produce the highest response rates and greatest resistance to extinction. Duolingo's leaderboard resets weekly, creating recurring variable reward cycles.

techniques.title: Progressive Disclosure Onboarding
techniques.description: New users see exactly 3 options at signup (language, goal, proficiency). The first lesson teaches exactly 4 words. Grammar rules appear only after pattern recognition is established. This textbook application of Sweller's CLT keeps extraneous cognitive load near zero.
techniques.evidence: Duolingo's placement test alone reduced Day-1 churn by 12% (internal A/B test revealed in GDC 2023 talk). The 'no explanation first' approach maps directly to CLT's worked example effect.

techniques.title: Social Proof via Competitive Leagues
techniques.description: The league system (Bronze→Diamond) serves dual SDT needs: competence (visible progress through tiers) and relatedness (you're competing alongside 30 other learners). But it undermines autonomy — the system decides when you're promoted/demoted, and passive users get pushed out.
techniques.evidence: SDT research (Ryan & Deci, 2017): competitive structures boost short-term engagement but can undermine intrinsic motivation when perceived as controlling. Duolingo's league churn spike at Diamond tier suggests this tension.

techniques.title: The Day-14 Hook Model Decay Problem
techniques.description: Nir Eyal's Hook Model (Trigger→Action→Variable Reward→Investment) powers Duolingo's first 14 days brilliantly. But after ~Day 14, external triggers (push notifications) lose novelty, variable rewards become predictable, and the investment-trigger loop weakens. This is why Duolingo's 30-day retention (~35%) drops sharply from 7-day retention (~55%).
techniques.evidence: SensorTower 2025 data: Duolingo D7 retention 55%, D30 35%, D90 ~18%. The Hook Model was designed for habit formation, not sustained skill development — it needs a transition to intrinsic motivation that Duolingo hasn't fully solved.

strengths: Streak mechanics create powerful daily habit
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on loss aversion raises ethical questions
Day-14+ motivation transition needs intrinsic drivers
8-12 notifications/day for lapsed users approaches dark pattern territory
